periods.summary: In a hidden ruin in a Southeast Asian jungle, Or-Gaule replays footage of Stella destroying his Hiraga Reisen puppet and becomes fixated on possessing and corrupting her. He later appears in Quedolan's training facility, mocks the League's sanitized war system, and demonstrates overwhelming control through his Device Black Widow. Without moving, he manipulates Prince John into killing the Quedolan representatives and shattering his mind. He extends invisible threads across Quedolan, capturing soldiers, pregnant women, children, and others to create his Wonderland, setting the stage for the future Vermillion Battle.

periods.summary: Or-Gaule abandons Rebellion because he is bored and massacres its Alpine headquarters, puppeteering guards into killing themselves and using Killing Opera and Deus Ex Machina. Wallenshtein initially counters him, but Or-Gaule arranged help from Naseem, Ein, and B.B.; they murder most present Apostles and free themselves to pursue a new game. Or-Gaule's chosen game is Stella: because he loves the purity and anger he saw in her, he wants to break her by forcing her to kill family and friends and by destroying Vermillion and Quedland's trust. In Luxel he reveals he has turned the city and Quedland government into his toy box, controlled John into killing King Clef and the representative knights, and launched Quedland's army against Vermillion through relay nodes. Alice cuts off his arm and evacuates the heroes, but he reattaches it and proceeds. At Caldia, after his allies disrupt the battlefield, he appears with John, Lunaeyes, and a declaration that turns the conflict into a legal representative war while rejecting League intervention.

periods.summary: Or-Gaule appears with John and Lunaeyes above Caldia, presenting the legal claim that Quedland and Vermillion have agreed to a League-style representative war. He uses John as a puppet mouthpiece, then openly admits he wants to avoid League interference because it would spoil his play with Stella. He placates Naseem by allowing League members already in Vermillion to join the roster and uses Quedland citizens as leverage to make Nene accept the arrangement. He releases Lunaeyes, withdraws healthy soldiers, orders Ein away from the palace, and sets conditions: a five-person battle royale in Quedland's capital with Stella as a mandatory Vermillion participant. Later discussion implies Lunaeyes paid him a terrible private price beyond ordinary advantage.

periods.summary: Or-Gaule contacts Naseem after the League border massacre, praises his victory over Carlo, and explains that the League army is effectively neutralized, though Naseem warns him not to interrupt his fight with Nene. At the start of the war Or-Gaule lets the battle split into personal duels. He confronts Alice by staging puppet reenactments of the Bloody Cross victims, including a doll resembling Alice herself begging him to stop. He enjoys Alice's rage and frames their fight as a continuation of the original massacre. In combat, Or-Gaule relies on invisible Black Widow threads spread through Luxel to create aerial footholds, evade Alice's stronger body, launch Killing Opera thread slashes, and hurl buildings with Deus Ex Machina. He also constantly talks about the murdered villagers with apparent affection, wounding Alice psychologically. After luring her through his thread nest, he attempts Marionette, but Alice's destiny-level fixation on killing him prevents control. His attacks cannot penetrate Invincible Armor, so he uses threads around her neck that tighten with her own movement. Even this only slows her: Alice throws her axe, predicts his escape, crushes both hands, and nearly strangles him. He escapes by manipulating threads with his toes after Alice spasms from suffocation, but Stella intercepts him in the sky and declares him one of the people better dead before releasing Salamander flame.
